nodes.title: Demerger: A strategic leap
nodes.summary:
Demerger: A strategic leap
To empower each business to pursue its distinct vision, the demerger of Tata Motors into two listed entities — Commercial Vehicles and Passenger Vehicles (including EV and JLR) — is progressing as planned. Enabling
08corporate actions to streamline the capital structure of the Company and enhance its operational focus gathered pace during the year with the successful delisting of its DVRs and the merger of Tata Motors Finance Ltd. with Tata Capital Ltd. In early FY26, your Company’s shareholders approved the demerger which is expected to be effective during the second half of 2025, with shareholders receiving equivalent shares in both entities.
The proposed demerger, will bring greater strategic clarity and agility, enabling a more focused approach to execution and value creation, delivering superior experiences for customers, rewarding careers for employees, and long‑term returns for shareholders.

nodes.title: 5 Supply chain disruptions and commodity price fluctuations
nodes.summary:
5 Supply chain disruptions and commodity price fluctuations
Operational
Our ability to supply components, in time, to our manufacturing operations is of paramount importance in achieving production schedules and meeting consumer demand. Commodity price fluctuations, being a major part of overall costs, might impact the cost competitiveness and overall profitability. Lastly, the volatile nature of the regulatory landscape (Tariffs) could also result in significant direct and indirect impacts to suppliers and disruption to logistics that increase production costs and lead times.

nodes.title: (i) Market risk:
nodes.summary:
(i) Market risk:
Market risk is the risk of any loss in future earnings, in realizable fair values or in future cash flows that may result from a change in the price of a financial instrument. The value of a financial instrument may change as a result of changes in the interest rates, foreign currency exchange rates, equity price fluctuations, liquidity and other market changes. Future specific market movements cannot be normally predicted with reasonable accuracy.

nodes.title: (a) Foreign exchange currency rate risk:
nodes.summary: The text addresses foreign exchange currency rate risk, noting that fluctuations can impact consolidated financial statements when transactions involve multiple currencies or assets/liabilities are in non-functional currencies. It identifies key currencies (U.S. dollar, GBP, Chinese renminbi, Japanese yen, Singapore dollar, Euro) and operational risks from exchange rate fluctuations. The company uses derivatives to hedge foreign exchange and interest rate exposure per its risk management policy. It explains that functional currency weakening may increase import and borrowing costs, affecting financing for capital expenditures. The company evaluates exchange rate risk impact through sensitivity analysis, calculating a 10% shift per currency. It presents foreign currency exposure tables (financial assets and liabilities) as of March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, with a 10% appreciation/depreciation potentially affecting net profit/(loss) and equity before tax by approximately ₹5,280 crores and ₹10,599 crores for financial assets and liabilities, respectively, for 2025. The exposure is mitigated by natural hedges and derivative contracts.

nodes.title: (b) Interest rate risk
nodes.summary: The text defines interest rate risk as the potential for changes in market rates to affect fair value, interest income/expense, and cash flows. It details the Company's exposure through variable-rate interest-bearing liabilities, primarily debt obligations, and its use of short-term bonds and loans for liquidity. It describes risk management strategies including matching funding maturities and rates, securitization of receivables, and interest rate swap contracts. Quantitative data shows financial liabilities subject to variable rates were ₹14,992 crores and ₹42,719 crores as of March 31, 2025 and 2024, with a 100 basis point shift impacting profit before tax by ₹150 crores and ₹427 crores, respectively. The methodology notes assumptions of instantaneous parallel yield curve shifts, potential non-corresponding reactions, lag effects, and constant other variables. It also mentions cross currency interest rate swaps used to hedge variable-rate foreign currency debt and convert fixed-rate foreign debt to floating.

Equity Price Risk is related to the change in market reference price of the investments in equity securities. The fair value of some of the Company’s investments in equity securities exposes the Company to equity price risks. In general, these securities are not held for trading purposes. These investments are subject to changes in the market price of securities.
The fair value of some of the Company’s investment in quoted equity securities measured at FVOCI as of March 31, 2025 and 2024, was ₹ 848 crores and ₹ 961 crores, respectively. A 10% change in prices of these securities held as of March 31, 2025 and 2024, would result in a pre-tax impact of ₹ 85 crores
and ₹ 96 crores on equity, respectively.

nodes.summary: The text provides an ageing analysis of trade and finance receivables as of March 31, 2025 and 2024, categorizing them into undisputed and disputed, considered good, significant increase in credit risk, and credit impaired, with allowances for expected credit losses. It notes trade receivables are spread across geographies with ongoing credit evaluation, and overdue amounts from Indian Government organizations are considered recoverable. Finance receivables' allowance is based on expected future collections adjusted for macroeconomic factors like GDP growth, fuel price, and inflation.

nodes.title: (iii) Liquidity risk
nodes.summary: The text defines liquidity risk as the risk of difficulty meeting financial obligations and outlines the objective of maintaining sufficient liquidity. It details the Company's funding sources, including bank working capital lines, debt markets (commercial paper, non-convertible debentures, fixed deposits, senior notes), and investments of surplus funds in low-risk bank deposits and mutual funds. It notes that 15% of public deposits/non-convertible debentures maturing within 12 months are held in bank deposits to meet regulatory liquidity norms. The Company monitors debt and capital market funding options for financial flexibility. It also provides tables of undiscounted contractual maturities of financial liabilities (trade payables, borrowings, lease liability, derivative liabilities, other financial liabilities) as of March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, showing carrying amounts and cash flows due in the 1st year, 2nd year, 3rd to 5th year, and after 5th year.

nodes.title: (iv) Derivative financial instruments and risk management
nodes.summary: The text covers the Company's use of derivative financial instruments for risk management, including foreign currency, interest rate, and commodity forwards and options, as well as interest rate swaps and cross currency swaps to hedge debt exposures. It lists specific transactional risks such as liquidity, pricing, interest rate, exchange rate, volatility, counterparty, settlement, and gearing risks. It details the fair value of derivatives as of March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, and provides a sensitivity analysis showing the impact of 10% foreign currency depreciation and appreciation on hedging reserves and profit and loss.

nodes.title: (v) Commodity Price Risk
nodes.summary: The section covers commodity price risk exposure to aluminium, copper, platinum, and palladium, including mitigation via derivatives and fixed-price contracts, hedge accounting for JLR, fair value gains/losses, and sensitivity analysis. It details cash flow hedges for foreign exchange, interest rate risk (SOFR swaps), commodity price risk, and net investment hedge. It also presents segment information for automotive (Tata Commercial Vehicles, Tata Passenger Vehicles, Jaguar Land Rover, Vehicle Financing), IT services, and insurance broking, with revenues, results, assets, liabilities, reconciliations, geographic and product disclosures, related-party transactions, earnings per share, Schedule III additional information, other statutory information, discontinued operations, and other notes.

nodes.title: (v) Commodity Price Risk (intro)
nodes.summary: The text covers commodity price risk exposure to aluminium, copper, platinum, and palladium, mitigated via derivatives and fixed-price contracts; JLR applied hedge accounting to aluminium and copper derivatives from January 1, 2025, while others are fair value through profit or loss. It reports fair value losses/gains on non-hedged commodity derivatives for 2025 and 2024, and sensitivity analysis showing the impact of a 10% price change on other comprehensive income and profit or loss. It details cash flow hedges for foreign exchange risk (various currencies and maturities), interest rate risk (SOFR swaps), commodity price risk, and related nominal amounts, carrying values, and average strike rates. It also includes a net investment hedge in GBP and segment reporting, primarily automotive with sub-segments Tata Commercial Vehicles, Tata Passenger Vehicles, Jaguar Land Rover, and Vehicle Financing.

It includes entity-wide disclosures by geography and product, related-party transactions (Tata Sons, subsidiaries, joint ventures, associates, key management compensation), transactions with struck-off companies, earnings per share (basic/diluted for continuing and discontinued operations), Schedule III additional information for subsidiaries/associates/joint ventures, other statutory information (Benami property, crypto, loans to ultimate beneficiaries, willful defaulter, layers, revaluation), discontinued operation (merger of Tata Motors Finance with Tata Capital), and other notes (demerger scheme, JLR stake disposal).

nodes.title: Opinion
nodes.summary: The section presents the auditor's report on Tata Motors Limited's standalone financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2025. It addresses management's and board's responsibilities, auditor's responsibilities, and other information. It also reports on legal and regulatory requirements under the Companies (Auditor's Report) Order, 2020, including pending litigations, long-term contracts, a delay in transferring funds to the Investor Education and Protection Fund (Rs. 0.08 crores), fund representations, dividend compliance, and exceptions in audit trail implementation. Additionally, it covers compliance with Section 197 on director remuneration, property records, loans and advances, deposits, statutory dues, loan repayment defaults, fraud reporting, whistleblower complaints, related party transactions, internal audit systems, and confirms no cash losses or auditor resignation.

It reports on loans, advances, and guarantees given, including overdue amounts from subsidiaries and suppliers, and compliance with Sections 185 and 186. nodes.title: Opinion

The document defines internal financial controls and notes their inherent limitations. It also includes the standalone financial statements: balance sheet, statement of profit and loss, cash flow statement, statement of changes in equity, and notes covering accounting policies, property plant and equipment, leases, intangible assets, investments, loans, inventories, trade receivables, cash, equity share capital, and other components of equity.

nodes.title: ii) Determination of fair value:
nodes.summary:
ii) Determination of fair value:
Fair value is the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date, regardless of whether that price is directly observable or estimated using another valuation technique. The fair value of a financial instrument on initial recognition is normally the transaction price (fair value of the consideration given or received). In estimating the fair value of an asset or liability, the Company takes into account the characteristics of the asset or liability if market participants would take those characteristics into account when pricing the asset or liability at the measurement date. Subsequent to initial recognition, the Company determines the fair value of financial instruments that are quoted in active markets using the quoted bid prices (financial assets held) or quoted ask prices (financial liabilities held) and using valuation techniques for other instruments. Valuation techniques include discounted cash flow method and other valuation methods.

nodes.title: iii) Derecognition of financial assets and financial liabilities:
nodes.summary: The text outlines derecognition principles for financial assets and liabilities. Financial assets are derecognized when contractual cash flow rights expire or when the asset is transferred with substantially all risks and rewards. If risks and rewards are neither transferred nor retained but control continues, a retained interest and associated liability are recognized. If substantially all risks and rewards are retained, the asset continues to be recognized with a collateralized borrowing for proceeds. Gains or losses on derecognition go to profit or loss; cumulative equity gains or losses are transferred to profit or loss, except for equity instruments elected at fair value through OCI, which go to retained earnings. Assets are written off when recovery is not reasonably expected, subject to review and possible enforcement. Financial liabilities are derecognized when extinguished, discharged, cancelled, or expired.

nodes.title: iv) Impairment of financial assets:
nodes.summary:
iv) Impairment of financial assets:
The Company recognises a loss allowance for expected credit losses on a financial asset that is at amortised cost or at fair value through other comprehensive income. Expected credit losses are forward looking and are measured in a way that is unbiased and represents a probability-weighted amount, takes into account the time value of money (values are discounted using the applicable effective interest rate) and uses reasonable and supportable information.

nodes.title: v) Hedge accounting:

Derivatives are initially and subsequently measured at fair value, with changes generally in profit or loss. It covers documentation of economic relationships, risk management objectives, and designation of intrinsic value for options and exclusion of foreign currency basis spreads. Effective hedge changes are recognized in other comprehensive income (cash flow hedge reserve), with ineffective portions in profit or loss. Amounts in equity are reclassified to profit or loss or balance sheet when forecast transactions occur. Forward premium and time value are treated as hedge costs, with changes in other comprehensive income. Effective interest rate swap changes are in other comprehensive income. Discontinuation rules are described, including reclassification of accumulated amounts and treatment of forecast transactions no longer expected to occur.
